llm_adjudication.requirement_a: Bij een verplichting uit het eerste lid die betrekking heeft op reeds in gebruik zijnde producten en diensten voor de aangewezen onderdelen, moet de bevoegde minister in het belang van de continuïteit een termijn vaststellen voor vervanging respectievelijk beëindiging daarvan.
llm_adjudication.requirement_b: De minister moet een private ontsluitende dienst toelaten door erkenning wanneer dit noodzakelijk is voor de continuïteit van de elektronische dienstverlening en de dienst aan de gestelde eisen inzake werking, beveiliging en betrouwbaarheid voldoet.
llm_adjudication.compliant_alternative: De minister kan een vervangingstermijn vaststellen voor bestaande producten of diensten en tegelijk, indien noodzakelijk en aan de eisen voldaan is, een private ontsluitende dienst erkennen. De erkenning kan als continuïteitsoplossing dienen tijdens of na de vervanging; de bepalingen verplichten niet om dezelfde dienst zowel onmiddellijk te beëindigen als onmiddellijk toe te laten.
llm_adjudication.unresolved_exception: Onopgelost is of de private ontsluitende dienst zelf een reeds in gebruik zijnde dienst is waarop de verplichting uit artikel 21a, eerste lid, betrekking heeft, en of een erkenning daarvan verenigbaar is met een eventuele verplichting tot beëindiging. llm_adjudication.outcome_changing_facts: De uitkomst zou kunnen veranderen als vaststaat dat artikel 21a, eerste lid, de minister verplicht juist dezelfde private ontsluitende dienst onmiddellijk te beëindigen, terwijl artikel 9 onder dezelfde omstandigheden verplicht die dienst toe te laten en geen overgangs- of vervangingsmogelijkheid bestaat.

llm_adjudication.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose mutually exclusive duties on the same actor for the same trigger: Norm A concerns supplying specified information to a central contact point, while Norm B concerns maintaining and providing immediate personnel access to a secondary processing location. llm_adjudication.requirement_a: Norm A requires domain-name registration service providers to provide the information referred to in Article 47(3) to the central contact point, using the established mechanism, for the ENISA register.
llm_adjudication.requirement_b: Norm B requires the controller to take appropriate measures so that the data subject receives GDPR Articles 13–14 information and Articles 15–22 and 34 communications concerning processing in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form and in clear and plain language.
llm_adjudication.compliant_alternative: The entity can provide the ENISA information through the prescribed mechanism while separately giving any affected data subject the required GDPR information or communication in the required accessible form. If the ENISA submission contains personal data, it can, where legally and factually appropriate, use data minimisation, anonymisation or pseudonymisation and restrict disclosure to the prescribed recipient; the text does not show that these measures are prohibited or that the ENISA submission replaces the GDPR communication.
llm_adjudication.unresolved_exception: It is unresolved whether the Article 47(3) information includes personal data, whether the entity is the GDPR controller for that processing, and whether any GDPR restriction or other legal basis limits disclosure to the central contact point. The provisions supplied contain no express reconciliation or exception addressing that overlap.
llm_adjudication.outcome_changing_facts: A contradiction could become plausible only if Article 47(3) required disclosure of specific personal data in a way that necessarily violated a binding GDPR prohibition, with no lawful minimisation, anonymisation, restricted-disclosure or other compliance route, or if the same communication had to be both withheld and disclosed to the same recipient for the same trigger.
llm_adjudication.criterion_fired: The texts establish potentially overlapping obligations but do not establish the factual and legal predicates needed to determine whether both apply to the same actor and data, or whether a compliant alternative is available; therefore a firm contradiction or non-conflict finding would require guessing.

llm_adjudication.shared_actor: Potentially a CSIRT that is also an authority or public body referred to in Article 77(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, but the texts do not establish that overlap.
llm_adjudication.shared_circumstance: The CSIRT obtains or handles information about cyber threats, vulnerabilities, or incidents and, where applicable, that information or documentation is obtained by an Article 77(1) authority or public body. Norm A additionally concerns dissemination, nearly in real time where possible; Norm B concerns subsequent processing under confidentiality duties.
llm_adjudication.requirement_a: Norm A requires CSIRTs to provide early warnings, notifications and announcements and disseminate information about cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents to affected essential and important entities, competent authorities and other relevant stakeholders, nearly in real time where possible.
llm_adjudication.requirement_b: Norm B requires information or documentation obtained by the Article 77(1) public authorities or bodies under Article 77 to be processed in accordance with the confidentiality obligations described in Article 78.
llm_adjudication.compliant_alternative: A CSIRT can disseminate only information compatible with the applicable confidentiality obligations—for example, restricted or anonymised information, or disclosures limited to authorised recipients—and then process any obtained information in accordance with Article 78. Norm A itself limits near-real-time performance to cases where possible.
llm_adjudication.unresolved_exception: The text supplied does not state the content or scope of Article 78 confidentiality obligations, nor whether they permit the particular dissemination required by Article 11(b), or establish that a CSIRT is an Article 77(1) authority or public body. Any specific confidentiality exception, recipient restriction, or priority rule remains unresolved.
llm_adjudication.outcome_changing_facts: The verdict could change if Article 78 expressly prohibited every disclosure required by Article 11(b), without permitting restricted, anonymised, authorised, or otherwise compliant disclosure, and the same CSIRT were subject to both provisions for the same information and trigger. It could also change if Article 78 expressly reconciled or deferred to Article 11.
llm_adjudication.criterion_fired: The provisions do not establish a contradiction, and joint compliance appears plausible through controlled disclosure, but the missing Article 78 text and unproven actor overlap prevent a firm verdict.

The lead overseer must also consult the oversight forum before exercising the powers referred to in paragraph 1.
llm_adjudication.requirement_b: A national authority or body responsible for monitoring or enforcing Union-law fundamental-rights obligations concerning the use of listed high-risk AI systems is empowered to request and inspect documentation prepared or maintained under the AI Act, in an accessible language and format, when access is necessary for effective exercise of its mandate; it must notify the relevant market-surveillance authority of the request.
